policy: Primary measurement is preferred. Restricted or unstable services remain explicit manual/adaptor boundaries. Secondary commentary never substitutes silently for failed primary data.

sources.name: Bureau of Labor Statistics
sources.notes: Automated public time-series API for CPI, earnings, household/labour and JOLTS series.

sources.name: Federal Reserve Board
sources.notes: SHED, Financial Accounts and other Board releases; add structured adapters only where redistribution and methodology are clear.

sources.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
sources.notes: SCE expectations and Consumer Credit Panel/QHDC; preserve survey fieldwork and quarterly reference periods.

sources.name: Bureau of Economic Analysis
sources.notes: Personal income, disposable income, PCE and saving rate.

sources.name: US Census Bureau
sources.notes: Household Pulse/Income and Poverty/retail series where methodologically appropriate.

sources.name: University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers
sources.notes: Current Conditions and Expectations. Respect licensing/redistribution terms; store only permitted measures with release metadata.

sources.name: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Survey
sources.notes: Present Situation, Expectations and labour differential. Respect licensing/redistribution terms.

sources.name: Pew Research Center
sources.notes: Political/economic attitudes; record exact fieldwork, sample and question wording.

sources.name: Gallup
sources.notes: Economy ratings, most important problem and approval. Preserve fieldwork dates and population.

sources.name: AP-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research
sources.notes: National probability-based polling; use original toplines/methodology.

sources.name: KFF
sources.notes: Health costs, affordability and issue attitudes.

sources.name: American National Election Studies
sources.notes: Election-study panel/cross-section; structural rather than high-frequency where applicable.

sources.name: Cooperative Election Study
sources.notes: Large-sample election study; use appropriate weighting and cycle metadata.

sources.name: Ipsos KnowledgePanel
sources.notes: Probability-based online panel; retain sponsor/instrument information.

sources.name: NORC AmeriSpeak
sources.notes: Probability-based panel; retain question wording and fieldwork.

sources.name: USC Understanding America Study
sources.notes: Longitudinal household panel useful for within-person movement.

sources.name: RAND American Life Panel
sources.notes: Longitudinal internet panel; structural/episodic use.

sources.name: JPMorgan Chase Institute
sources.notes: De-identified transaction/cash-buffer research; population coverage differs from national surveys.

sources.name: Bank of America Institute
sources.notes: Card/transactional indicators; label customer-base coverage and nominal/real adjustments.

sources.name: Federal Reserve Consumer Credit Panel
sources.notes: Credit-bureau panel and Household Debt and Credit reports.

sources.name: Credit-bureau aggregate datasets
sources.notes: Only named, documented aggregates may be ingested; never synthesize unavailable bureau data.

sources.name: Public card-spending datasets
sources.notes: Use only documented public series with population/coverage metadata.

sources.name: Mortgage/auto delinquency datasets
sources.notes: Prefer official/credit-panel aggregates; separate categories and transition rates.

sources.name: Center for American Progress
sources.notes: Interpretation only. Claims must retain empirical basis, causal claim, policy frame and evidence strength.

sources.name: Brookings Institution
sources.notes: Interpretation only; not ground truth.

sources.name: Economic Policy Institute
sources.notes: Interpretation only; preserve policy assumptions.

sources.name: American Enterprise Institute
sources.notes: Interpretation only; preserve policy assumptions.

sources.name: Urban Institute
sources.notes: Interpretation only; preserve empirical/causal separation.

sources.name: Harvard Joint Center for Housing Studies
sources.notes: Housing interpretation/structural evidence; publication dates may be recent while reference data are older.
